R names its [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function)s by a prefix that says what the function computes,
followed by a short name for the family (@tbl-r-prefixes and @tbl-r-families).

| Prefix | Computes | Example |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `d` | the [mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) or [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) | `dnorm()` |
| `p` | the [cumulative distribution function](random-variables.qmd#def-cdf) | `pnorm()` |
| `q` | the [quantile function](random-variables.qmd#def-quantile-function) | `qnorm()` |
| `r` | [random](notation.qmd#def-random) draws | `rnorm()` |

: Prefixes of R's [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function) names, with the [Gaussian](random-variables.qmd#def-normal) family as the example. {#tbl-r-prefixes}

| Family | R name | Parameters, in R's order |
|:--|:--|:--|
| [Bernoulli](random-variables.qmd#def-bernoulli) | `binom` with `size = 1` | `prob` |
| [Binomial](#def-binomial) | `binom` | `size`, `prob` |
| [Poisson](#def-poisson) | `pois` | `lambda` |
| [Uniform](random-variables.qmd#def-uniform) | `unif` | `min`, `max` |
| [Gaussian](random-variables.qmd#def-normal) | `norm` | `mean`, `sd` |
| [Exponential](random-variables.qmd#def-exponential) | `exp` | `rate` |

: R names for some families in this chapter. {#tbl-r-families}

R has no separate [Bernoulli](random-variables.qmd#def-bernoulli) family:
use the [binomial](#def-binomial) [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function)s with `size = 1`.
The next chunk evaluates each prefix for the standard [Gaussian distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-normal)
and for a [binomial distribution](#def-binomial) with three trials (@tbl-r-calls).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r-calls
#| tbl-cap: "The four prefixes applied to two families"
#| code-fold: false

set.seed(1)
gaussian_density <- dnorm(0)
gaussian_cdf <- pnorm(1.96)
gaussian_quantile <- qnorm(0.975)
gaussian_draw <- rnorm(1)
binomial_mass <- dbinom(2, size = 3, prob = 1 / 2)
binomial_cdf <- pbinom(2, size = 3, prob = 1 / 2)
binomial_quantile <- qbinom(0.5, size = 3, prob = 1 / 2)
binomial_draw <- rbinom(1, size = 3, prob = 1 / 2)

call_text <- c(
  "dnorm(0)",
  "pnorm(1.96)",
  "qnorm(0.975)",
  "rnorm(1)",
  "dbinom(2, size = 3, prob = 1 / 2)",
  "pbinom(2, size = 3, prob = 1 / 2)",
  "qbinom(0.5, size = 3, prob = 1 / 2)",
  "rbinom(1, size = 3, prob = 1 / 2)"
)

call_values <- c(
  gaussian_density,
  gaussian_cdf,
  gaussian_quantile,
  gaussian_draw,
  binomial_mass,
  binomial_cdf,
  binomial_quantile,
  binomial_draw
)

calls <- dplyr::tibble(call = call_text, value = call_values)

knitr::kable(calls, digits = 4)
```

The value of `dbinom(2, size = 3, prob = 1 / 2)` is $3/8 = 0.375$,
which matches the [two heads in three flips](#exm-binomial-pmf) example.
